bugs.root_cause: attrs.converters.optional() wraps a Converter returned by pipe(str, int) in a plain single-argument closure. The generated __init__ therefore calls optional_converter(value), and optional_converter calls the inner Converter with only value even though the Converter requires value, instance, and field. This causes a TypeError when Measurement("42") is constructed.

impacted_items.reason: This is the function containing the bug; optional() incorrectly handles a Converter object returned by pipe().
pipe() returns a Converter requiring value, instance, and field, which is incompatible with the current optional() wrapper.
The Converter call requires three arguments, but optional_converter currently supplies only the value.
It correctly wraps the plain optional_converter, but this wrapping exposes the incompatible single-argument call path.
This module re-exports optional from attr.converters, so the namespace is affected when the underlying implementation is fixed.
This is a namespace import with no converter logic of its own.

bugs.root_cause: ExpenseTracker.update_expense (api.py line 87-88) calls self.get_expense(expense_id), which returns None when the ID is not found. The very next line dereferences exp.title (if exp.title is None:) without first checking whether exp itself is None. This raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'title' instead of the intended ValueError('Expense ... not found.'). The fix is to guard with `if exp is None:` before touching any attribute of exp.

impacted_items.reason: This is the bug site; the missing None-check causes AttributeError to propagate to every caller instead of a clean ValueError.
get_expense correctly returns None for a missing ID, but the caller (update_expense) fails to handle that None return value.
cmd_update is the CLI entry point that calls update_expense; it propagates the uncaught AttributeError directly to the user as a raw traceback.
Existing test accepts both ValueError and AttributeError (`pytest.raises((ValueError, AttributeError))`), so it passes even with the bug present and provides weak coverage.
